name: Spatial Calibration & Geodetic Projection
purpose: Convert image-space detections into metric ground coordinates. Owns the planar homography projector, the ground-plane calibration fit and verification tool, and the BIM/IFC datum resolver used to place hazard geometry in the digital twin.

public_interfaces.name: HomographyProjector.project / project_box
public_interfaces.contract: Maps native-frame points to metric ground coordinates and reports a calibration-error estimate; never silently extrapolates outside the surveyed region.

public_interfaces.name: fit_ground_plane (survey-point least squares)
public_interfaces.contract: Accepts >= 4 surveyed correspondences, returns a homography plus residual RMSE; rejects degenerate configurations.

public_interfaces.name: BIMSpatialResolver.resolve
public_interfaces.contract: Resolves BIM entity references to geodetic boundaries for dynamic exclusion envelopes.

acceptance_criteria: A surveyed 4+ point calibration yields a homography and an explicit RMSE.
Projection of a known image marker lands within the calibrated tolerance on the ground plane.
BIM resolution degrades to a labelled unavailable state when ifcopenshell is absent.
Calibration artefacts are tied to a camera identity so a mismatch cannot be used silently.
risks: Calibration is the single largest accuracy risk in the product: every downstream metric (TTC, proximity, zone entry) inherits its error.
The default configuration ships example data; a production deployment must replace it with surveyed points or the twin is decorative.
